name: Rhombille
desc: A plane of tumbling blocks cut from the rhombille tiling — three rhombi to a hexagon, shaded as the three faces of a cube — with a reversal front sweeping across so the whole field turns inside out behind it, every block popping from raised to hollow as the seam glints past.

energy.doc: face contrast + joint weight + chiaroscuro depth

scale.doc: block size vs frame (2.2 = a few colossal cubes)

density.doc: reserved shading jitter across the field

flip.doc: strength of the Necker reversal front (0 = every cube reads the same way forever)

hatch.doc: engraved ruling along each face's own axis

x.doc: field centre x as canvas fraction

y.doc: field centre y as canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: three-ruling copperplate engraving on bone / two-ink risograph / pieced folk quilt / raking-light brutalist concrete / luminous additive wireframe on black (non-representational)
